sections.title: Measurement outcomes and the Born rule
sections.question: How does a declared projective measurement map a normalized state to probabilities for classical outcome labels?
sections.exit: StatefiniteprojectiveBornruleaspostulate;derivepositivity andnormalization;translatecomputational labels,marginals andcoarse outcomes without confusingprobabilities withsamples orstateupdates.

sections.title: Conditional states and ignored outcomes
sections.question: Given a declared ideal projective update, what state is assigned to a selected nonzero branch, and how are later probabilities computed when its outcome is ignored?
sections.entry: 6.1 pure global states, orthogonal complete projectors and Born probabilities; normalized conditional vector is an additional ideal-update assumption.
sections.exit: Prove branch normalization, repeatability, ordered sequential joint and ignored-outcome marginal probabilities; distinguish coarse projection from fine measurement with a forgotten record, without averaging vectors.
sections.worked_case: Complex qubit; ordered register masks; Bell correlations; Z-then-plus interference; parity-versus-fine within-event coherence.
sections.boundary: Pure global inputs and finite projectors; branch enumeration is classical postprocessing of an actual simulated preparation. No native collapse or shots, no mixed-state operator update before Chapter 8.
sections.code_plan: Use released native FQ preparation and exact computational probability queries; explicit branch/joint helpers with zero/rare-event contracts.
sections.independent_check: Scalar coordinate masks, closed phase formulas, independently indexed prepared states and unnormalized ordered projector products.
sections.transfer_task: New nonadjacent four-qubit selections and complex Fourier rank-two projections.

sections.title: Observables, spectra, and expectations
sections.question: How do real spectral outcome values and Born probabilities produce an expectation, and how does that identity map to native FlagQuantum observables?

sections.exit: Prove the weighted-spectral/quadratic identity, reality, spectral bounds and real linearity; distinguish outcome, expectation, correlated product and measurement protocol.
sections.worked_case: Z readout; complex Pauli-Y signs; tilted H; degenerate ZZ; reversed nonadjacent Pauli support; noncommuting sum and affine units.
sections.boundary: Finite normalized pure inputs and Hermitian observables; native real Pauli sums, explicit classical spectra. No general hardware readout protocol, variance/shot statistics or mixed-state expectations.
sections.code_plan: Actual fq.expectation named requests and result.expectation; @ on disjoint observables, * real scalar; dense and explicit-projector checks.
sections.independent_check: Closed one-qubit amplitudes/means and analytic H projectors; scalar parity sums; indexed preparations and numerical spectral reconstructions.
sections.transfer_task: New complex Hermitian two-qubit Pauli sum and reversed nonadjacent four-qubit support.

sections.title: From exact probabilities to samples
sections.question: How do native terminal bit records give unbiased event, categorical and score estimates without confusing a record with its probability law?
sections.entry: 6.1 Born probabilities; a local finite classical probability/expectation bridge is supplied.
sections.exit: Prove IID product law, indicator and categorical means, score mean and multinomial count law; distinguish unbiasedness from independence or a confidence guarantee.
sections.worked_case: Ry Bernoulli; reversed nonadjacent correlated register labels; exact rational ensembles and rare/dependent/drifting counterexamples.
sections.boundary: Finite IID trials, fixed known readout, no postselection. Variance and confidence in 6.7-6.8; no inferred collapse or hardware IID guarantee.
sections.code_plan: Native fq.probabilities and fq.samples with shots and seed; explicit integer histogram; independent rational enumeration.
sections.independent_check: Analytic Ry probabilities, scalar full-state indices, explicit Python counts and exact Fraction ensemble means.
sections.transfer_task: Fresh four-qubit nonadjacent selections, new angles/seeds and rational categorical score.

sections.title: Variance, covariance, and uncertainty
sections.question: Which covariance terms determine the uncertainty of a weighted measurement estimator, and when may independent-group variances be added?
sections.entry: 6.3 spectral mean;6.6 finite expectation, IID law and unbiased frequencies.
sections.exit: Prove centered covariance expansion and weighted variance; derive IID mean/categorical covariance and independent-setting formulas; derive unbiased sample covariance and state its limits.
sections.worked_case: Complex Ry/P qubit with A=.7X-.4Z; correlated/anticorrelated pair readout; categorical one-hot covariance; separate X/Z settings; rare zero record and common offset.
sections.boundary: Finite second moments, fixed real weights, specified joint records and inter-trial/group independence. No confidence interval, shot allocation optimum, hardware-IID guarantee or general uncertainty-principle theorem.
sections.code_plan: Native fq.expectation, exact probabilities and terminal samples; original centered covariance helpers; no invented native variance endpoint.
sections.independent_check: Spectral/dense centered vector and analytic A²; joint scalar correlations; exact Fraction ensemble means and covariance; sample score versus covariance forms.
sections.transfer_task: Fresh complex four-qubit nonadjacent records, new one-qubit observables and independent setting pair.

sections.title: Confidence intervals and shot budgets

sections.entry: 6.7 covariance, IID mean variance and random estimated standard error.
sections.exit: Prove Markov, Chebyshev, bounded-range variance and conservative integer shot bound; distinguish fixed-parameter coverage, random intervals, exact binomial endpoints and invalid plug-in/adaptive rules.

sections.boundary: Fixed design and positive epsilon/delta; certified population variance bound; IID or explicit estimator variance model. No posterior, hardware calibration, optional-stopping, interval inversion or optimal allocation guarantee.
